Privacy review 2026-08-20, external sign-off record held by the release owner, extended by the release owner on 2026-08-22 to cover PR #44. Device-local storage; Sentry PII scrubbing verified by operations.test; AU-appropriate monitoring. NO REAL IDENTITY TRANSMITTED. PR #44 made /api/acceptance/sentry routable for the first time; that route calls Sentry setUser with a deliberately synthetic identity (id is the request sentinel, email is <sentinel>@invalid.example, a reserved non-routable TLD). Verified at this commit: the route is pinned to NEXT_PUBLIC_ANCHOR_ENV === 'preview' at build time so beta and production builds contain no live route; it reads request headers only and never parses a request body; and it is additionally gated by a smoke-acceptance build flag, a bearer-token gate worker, and an anchor-smoke-[a-f0-9]{32} sentinel format check. RESIDUAL RISK ACCEPTED: the preview pin is build-time inlined, so it is a build-configuration guarantee rather than a runtime one. SEPARATE NOTE ADDED 2026-08-23: the beta rehearsal worker's HTTP Basic gate does not cover /assets/*, by deliberate design (routing static files through the wrapper 404s the app's JS and CSS). Hashed asset filenames are only discoverable via the gated HTML, so exposure is low, but the gate is not a complete access control and should be described that way to reviewers. END-TO-END EVIDENCE OBTAINED 2026-08-23, FIRST TIME EVER: acceptance runs #20 and #21 delivered a real synthetic event to Sentry from the Worker and read it back through Sentry's API. The application-side scrubbing works exactly as lib/sentry-privacy.ts claims - every field the application could populate came back NULL (id, email, username, name, data), and the synthetic sentinel did not reach Sentry. Until today this rested on operations.test asserting over source strings; it now rests on an event that actually made the round trip. DISCOVERED AFTER THIS APPROVAL WAS GIVEN, AND NOT COVERED BY IT: the same event carried user.ip_address and a user.geo object derived from it. The application did not send these and cannot remove them - sendDefaultPii is already false and beforeSend already deletes event.user outright on all three runtimes. Sentry's INGESTION attaches them from the connection that delivered the envelope, which is also why tags reappear after scrubSentryEvent deletes them. The only effective control is the Sentry project setting Security & Privacy > 'Prevent Storing of IP Addresses', which is an account action for the release owner. THIS IS RECORDED AS AN OPEN RISK, NOT AS APPROVED. The release owner has not been asked to accept client IP storage and derived geolocation, and should not be taken to have done so by the presence of this paragraph.

approvals.reviewer: independent accessibility review, including disabled and ADHD participants
approvals.evidence_ref: Independent accessibility review 2026-08-23, report held by the release owner - conflicts declared, disabled and ADHD participants included per issue #12. Reviewer identities are deliberately not recorded here: the schema forbids committing reviewer signatures or personal contact information, and participants with lived experience of disability or an eating disorder must not be identifiable from a git repository. AUTOMATED HALF, verified separately and reproducibly at this commit - and note it did not exist before 2026-08-23, when an exhaustive search found no accessibility tooling anywhere in this repository, meaning the 2026-08-04 record's identical claim described a check that had never run: (1) eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y, the 31 rules its recommended set enables, promoted to ERROR on every file that can contain JSX, inside the existing lint step - previously jsx-a11y arrived only transitively via eslint-config-next, caught 1 of 6 deliberate violations, and reported warnings, so lint exited 0 regardless. (2) tests/accessibility.test.mjs - axe-core over the HTML the built Worker actually renders, WCAG 2.1 A/AA, in the quality gate on every push and pull request. (3) scripts/a11y-browser.mjs and the Accessibility (real browser) workflow - axe in headless Chromium at a 390x844 phone viewport with the real stylesheet applied, so COLOUR CONTRAST is genuinely evaluated; jsdom cannot do this. Result: 0 violations in both harnesses, 18 passing checks in the browser run, confirmed green in CI. Each harness carries a self-check that runs it over deliberately broken markup and fails if it does not object, so a green tick cannot mean 'the checker did nothing'. THE BROWSER RUN EARNED ITS PLACE IMMEDIATELY: it found two real defects the jsdom suite could not see, both aria-label on a bare div, where the implicit role of 'generic' prohibits the attribute. On .progress-dots the onboarding step indicator was announcing NOTHING to screen-reader users despite a correctly written label; fixed with role='img'. On .brand a redundant label made the announcement unpredictable; removed. Both fixed at this commit lineage before this approval. KNOWN LIMITS, STATED: colour contrast is evaluated only in the browser workflow, which is workflow_dispatch rather than per-push because it downloads Chromium and costs metered Actions time - run it whenever colours, focus styles or ARIA change and before any governed deploy. And no scanner measures cognitive load, working-memory demand, time blindness, task abandonment and re-entry, or whether the product shames its user; those rest entirely on the independent human review recorded above.

known_issues: OPEN, PRIVACY, NEEDS A RELEASE-OWNER DECISION: Sentry stores the client IP address and a derived geolocation for every event Anchor sends. Confirmed 2026-08-23 by reading a delivered event back through Sentry's API (acceptance run #21): user = { data:null, email:null, geo:object, id:null, ip_address:string, name:null, username:null }. The application is not the source - it sends no user object at all - so this cannot be fixed in code, and a beforeSend hook stripping those fields would be dead code deleting what is already deleted. The control is Sentry project settings > Security & Privacy > 'Prevent Storing of IP Addresses'. IMPACT TODAY IS EFFECTIVELY NIL: the beta is unlinked, noindex/nofollow, and has no users. It should be closed before any real person opens Anchor, because on an ADHD and eating-disorder wellbeing tool operated by an Australian health service an IP plus inferred location is personal information and is not something a client would expect to be leaving their device.

RESOLVED AT THIS PIN, AND THE REASON IT WAS FOUND MATTERS: wrangler.production.jsonc set run_worker_first: true, which routes every request including static files through the Worker. Deploy Anchor #2 shipped with it and REPORTED COMPLETE SUCCESS on every step, health check included, while the deployed app was unusable: every /assets/* request returned 503, no CSS or JS loaded, and the page sat on 'Finding a gentle place to begin' forever. /api/health is served by the Worker, so it answered correctly the whole time. wrangler.beta.jsonc already documented that this flag breaks the app's JS and CSS, and then asserted that production 'keeps run_worker_first: true because there the app worker itself is main and serves assets correctly' - an assertion nothing had ever tested, because deploy.yml had never run to completion. It was false. The flag is removed at this pin, and deploy.yml now fetches the rendered page and requires every /assets/ path it references to return 200, so this class of failure cannot report success again. NOTE: wrangler.smoke.jsonc still sets run_worker_first: true and its acceptance run also only checks /api/health, so the smoke harness carries the same blind spot and has not been changed here.

RESOLVED 2026-08-22 (PR #47), AND NOW VERIFIED END TO END on 2026-08-23 - acceptance runs #20 and #21 delivered a synthetic event from the Worker and read it back through Sentry's API, so the 503 delivery_failed described below no longer occurs. Retained for the record: Sentry.init never ran on the Cloudflare Worker, so the app had NO server-side error monitoring and POST /api/acceptance/sentry returned 503 delivery_failed. Root cause: instrumentation.ts gated the Sentry import on process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME being 'nodejs' or 'edge' - a stock-Next.js convention. Proven twice that nothing sets it here: zero matches for NEXT_RUNTIME across all 740 files of vinext@0.0.50, and dist/server/index.js reading it exactly twice and assigning it zero times. The gate was removed. The password-gated beta rehearsal deployed 2026-08-23 from this commit carries the fix, but a gated acceptance run returning 202 with an event id is still required to confirm delivery end to end.

OPEN, EVIDENCE INTEGRITY: FOUR separate green signals on this project have meant less than their labels - most seriously a complete-success deploy that shipped a white screen, described in the first known issue above, which is the only one of them to have reached a running environment - eight of ten operations tests asserted that code had been WRITTEN (regex over source strings) rather than that it worked, and two real defects survived weeks behind them (fixed by the behavioural tests in PR #48); the 'dependency review' workflow is a duplicate npm audit on a trigger that excludes main; and CodeQL passes while its findings are discarded. None of these was dishonest when introduced, but the release record has been citing them as independent evidence. A pending PR addresses the latter two.

OPEN: the Uptime workflow has no schedule and no configured healthcheck endpoints. PREVIEW_/BETA_/PRODUCTION_HEALTHCHECK_URL have never been set, and no environment has a stable URL to point them at. uptime_check cannot be satisfied until a governed deploy exists. The schedule was removed in PR #46 after a */15 cron with a three-job matrix exhausted the account's GitHub Actions allowance on 2026-08-22.

OPEN, NOT A DEFECT - SCOPE OBSERVATION: the built route table is one page ('/') plus /api/health and /api/acceptance/sentry, both of which exist only for CI to call. Zero files import db/; db/schema.ts declares no tables; there are no server actions and no dynamic route segments. The D1 binding, drizzle and the database are unused starter scaffolding. A local-first single-page app is carrying a Worker, a pre-0.1 shim, an image optimiser, an unused database, an acceptance gate worker and a smoke harness. Worth deciding deliberately rather than inheriting.
OPEN, LOW: actions/upload-artifact@v4 targets Node 20, which is deprecated and force-run on Node 24. Dependabot PR #4 proposes the bump.

decision.notes: CLEAN REPIN of anchor-v7-beta-2026-08-23b. That record was correct and its deploy worked - Deploy Anchor #5 shipped it and the app has been live and functioning since - but it pinned dbd22af, a commit whose deploy.yml did not parse. The broken YAML was mine, made editing the file in GitHub's browser editor, and repaired in the commit immediately after. Nothing shipped from it: the workflow definition comes from main, not from the checked-out tree, and only dist/ is deployed. It was still the wrong thing to leave in a governance record, because an auditor checking out the pinned commit finds a workflow file GitHub refused to load. WHAT THE PINNED TREE ADDS OVER dbd22af, NONE OF IT SHIPPED CODE: a parseable deploy.yml; scripts/deployed-asset-check.mjs and tests/deployed-asset-check.test.mjs, which give the deploy's asset gate the self-check every other harness in this repository has - seven tests, one of which reconstructs Deploy Anchor #2 (page renders, every asset 503) and asserts the gate refuses it; the package.json wiring that runs those on every push, taking the unit tier from 8 tests to 15; a corrected comment in wrangler.beta.jsonc, which until now asserted that production served assets correctly with run_worker_first on - the false sentence that let the white-screen deploy go unquestioned; .github/dependabot.yml pins for eslint 10 and @types/node 26 with their reasons; and a rewritten user-object check in scripts/verify-sentry-acceptance.mjs. NO COMPONENT, ROUTE, STYLE, TAXONOMY, SUPPORT-LIBRARY, MEAL-LIBRARY OR ECOSYSTEM-CONTRACT FILE DIFFERS FROM dbd22af, and none differs from 10dedbe either. The deployed artifact is byte-identical apart from the release SHA inlined at build time. Verifiable with git diff dbd22af..4ec9749 --stat. The six approvals are carried forward on the same basis as the previous record and are not re-sought. ONE NEW FINDING IS RECORDED AND IS NOT APPROVED. Server-side Sentry now works end to end, which is a genuine advance and the first real evidence that the privacy scrubbing does what it says. Reading a delivered event back also showed Sentry storing client IP and derived geolocation, which the application neither sends nor can remove. It is recorded as an open risk in this record and in the privacy evidence, it needs a Sentry account setting the release owner controls, and the presence of a paragraph describing it must not be read as the release owner having accepted it. SCOPE UNCHANGED: ungated beta only, noindex/nofollow, unlinked, no production record exists.
